ranking.note: Raised to P1: fixes a -reindex-chainstate startup race and stale-data-during-reorg window (category's top concern, correctness under reorgs) while being the stated prerequisite for out-of-process indexes (#10102) and shared chain sync (#15719); it cannot sit in the same band as the ordinary speedups it enables.
Moved up from score position 8: data integrity ranks first in this category and this is the index-scoped fix for corrupt/failed index reads being reported to users as 'transaction not found'.
Placed ahead of #26966 because it extracts the batching foundation that the parallel-sync PR builds on.
New index with a stated consumer ranks below integrity fixes and sync-time work per the category ordering, hence 4 places below its own score position.

inconsistencies: #35728 and #34132 attack the same underlying problem from different layers: corrupt or failed point reads surfacing as 'missing' data. #34132 makes dbwrapper point-read failures fatal globally; #35728 makes TxIndex/GetTransaction throw. Reviewers should settle the layer question once; review #35728 first (index-scoped, directly fixes the user-visible false 'not found'), then #34132, whose core is dbwrapper/coins and largely outside this category.

Chain: #34489 (batched index writes) is explicitly the extracted foundation for #26966 (parallel index sync); #34489 must be reviewed and settled first or #26966 will be rebased onto it anyway. #34489 itself depends on already-merged #34897.

#36002 (txindex in pruned mode) and #36480 (txospenderindex compact keys / block-sequence positions) both build on the #35531 key-format change and both move indexes toward pruned-mode support; #36002 establishes the pattern and the pruned-block error-data convention, so it should be reviewed before #36480.

#24230 and #35474 both restructure how indexes are owned and reached (interfaces and node::SyncChain vs. moving globals into NodeContext). They overlap in files and intent; #24230 is the broader, correctness-bearing change and should set the direction before #35474 is evaluated.

#36629 claims pruned-node operation for a new index while #36002 is still the open PR that establishes pruned-mode index support; the dependency is not stated on either card and should be clarified during review.
result.notes: The list spreads cleanly across bands: one framework/correctness PR that also unblocks the multiprocess project (P1), a solid P2 core of integrity fixes, sync-time work, and two user-facing index features, two internal housekeeping refactors (P3), and one logging-format cleanup (P4). No PR was downgraded; the only band change is #24230 upward.
